pr.title: Check the publish rules before a review loop starts
pr.head: 3ae818671ff588fcf21c1d20a669ca0e050763e5

summary: A review loop publishes reviews and pull request summaries from subagents with project review publish and project summary publish. A host's automatic approval, such as Claude Code's auto mode or Codex's approval reviewer, can refuse those commands unless the person's own settings allow them. project init, run by a person at a terminal, adds the allow rules. Until this change, nothing let an agent check for the rules first, so a loop learned that they were missing only when a publish was refused partway through.

This change adds project review rules, a read-only check. It prints allows or lacks for each settings file, and exits 0 when every file has the rules or 1 otherwise. start-review-loop runs it once before its first review and warns the user on exit 1, then keeps going.

1. The check reuses the report-only path of init. It calls allow_publish with apply=False, which reads each file and never writes.
  2. A new hint flag keeps commands out of its notes. With hint=False, the note for a missing rule no longer says to pass --publish-rule, because the agent running the check must not add the rules itself.
  3. The loop skill and the CLI reference document the check.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Publish rules: the allow rules Bash(project review publish *) and Bash(project summary publish *) in ~/.claude/settings.json, and Projector's rule file ~/.codex/rules/projector.rules where Codex is installed.
  • allow_publish: the function that init calls to add those rules, or with apply=False to report on them.
  • FileAction: one file's result, with an action such as unchanged or kept, and an optional note.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html: The Projector review of this head is clean, with no finding threads. It lists two suggestions: the closing line asks the user to add "the rules above" when only the Codex note, which names no rule, is above it, and a settings file that is not valid JSON gets a note saying the rules "were not added" though the check never tries to add them.

groups.title: The read-only check
groups.kicker: The new review rules subcommand and the hint flag it passes
intro: project review rules asks allow_publish to report on each settings file without writing. A file whose action is unchanged already has the rules and prints allows. Any other action, including a file that cannot be read, prints lacks. Each file's note goes to stderr after the file lines, followed by one closing line that asks the user to run project init in a terminal.
The hint flag defaults to true, so init keeps its notes as they were. Only the new check turns it off.

files.note: Adds the rules subparser with --json, and review_rules, which run_review calls before it reads any review state.

checks.text: The check writes nothing. Both allow_in_claude and allow_in_codex return before write_through when apply is false. The reviewer ran the command against a temporary home and found the tree unchanged after each run.
rules defines no --state-dir, --loop, or pull request number, so this early return must come before run_review reads those arguments.

files.note: Threads hint through allow_publish to the report-only notes for Claude Code and Codex.

checks.text: init's two callers of allow_publish pass no hint, so their notes still name --publish-rule. Python joins the adjacent string literals before it applies the conditional, so the suffix appears whole or not at all.
With hint=False, this Codex note names no rule, while the closing line in review_rules asks the user to "add the rules above". The Claude Code note does list its missing rules.

groups.title: The review loop runs the check
groups.kicker: start-review-loop checks once, warns once, and keeps going
intro: The check becomes step 2 of "Establish the loop". On exit 1 the loop tells the user, before the first review, that a publish can be refused and that running project init in a terminal adds the rules. A missing rule does not stop the loop, because the repository's own settings can still allow the commands.
A new bullet for subagents says a refused publish is never retried in another form, and the loop tells the user once for the loop rather than once for each pull request.

checks.text: The renumbering moves the one citation of a later step: "unreviewed in step 5" names the step that determines the last reviewed SHA. The reviewer searched the skills and docs for other citations of these step numbers and found none.

files.note: Adds the new step 2, renumbers the steps after it, and adds the bullet on refused publishes.

groups.title: Reference and tests
groups.kicker: The CLI reference entry and the tests that hold the check to writing nothing
intro: docs/cli.md documents the command's output, its --json fields, and its exit codes, and points to it from the init paragraph on publish rules. ReviewRulesTests runs the check through main() and compares every path and byte under a temporary home before and after each run.

checks.text: The reviewer ran the repository's gate at this head: 459 tests passed with one skip, project check passed, both claude plugin validate runs passed, and git diff --check was clean.

files.note: Adds ReviewRulesTests: rules present, missing, unreadable, a Codex directory without the rule file, and a pull request number as a usage error.
